stage1.impression: A warm, atmospheric long view of a timber-and-concrete bar with good depth and real pools of light. It still reads as a competent CG render, not a photograph. The whole frame has a sepia/orange cast. The floor carries blotchy, multiplied stool shadows. A hard theatrical ellipse of light on the right wall is the brightest surface in the room. The big smoked globe at the top reads as a dark, heavy mass, not as glowing cast acrylic. The speakers at the far end are tiny pale boxes, so no EARF product is the hero at a glance. As it stands, a magazine would see a handsome but fairly generic dark bar; the globe and the altar are the only things that make it specific, and neither reads yet.

blocking_9: Mother EARF must read as thick smoked cast acrylic: polished disc edges catching light, see-through tint, its shadow clearly a globe's shadow on the concrete, not a dark blob against the beams (region 620,10,860,270 lum_p95 >= 80 with crisp edge highlights)
The wall spot must stop being the brightest surface: the ellipse on the concrete (960,40,1060,500) should be lower than the bar top and grade off softly, not a theatre follow-spot
An EARF product must be the hero at a glance: either the altar pair larger in frame or the globe lit so its tint and edges carry the picture
Neutral warm-grey concrete, not beige/sepia: the grade should drop the orange cast so the only colour is the product's
Floor and props: a believable polished concrete floor without blotchy multiplied shadow patterns, and visible signs of life (coat, record, menu) in the foreground
The large framed screens on the right wall should glow softly; they should not read as flat pink-grey blank panels

defects.what: Mother EARF reads as a dark, almost opaque mass (lum_median 23.6, p95 51.6); the disc edges barely glow and it looks heavy, not like cast acrylic

Hard elliptical spot pool on the concrete wall, lum_median 108 with a 1 px hard edge (step 68); reads as a stage follow-spot. The globe's shadow inside it is a thin diagonal line, not legible as a globe
Large framed screen is a flat, uniform pink-grey panel (lum_median 116, range only 99) that reads as a blank light box
Second screen is also a blurry blank pink panel
Foreground floor too bright for a night room (median 84) and covered in blotchy, overlapping stool and table shadows like a caustic pattern; the concrete looks mottled and wet rather than polished
Altar speakers are tiny (about 40 px wide) and read as white boxes with grey woofers; the smoked acrylic cabinet barely registers
Bar top hot (median 145, p95 235) and brighter than the stated hero
Orbs read as flat white discs with no gradient or smoked tint; four identical copies in a row read as instanced
Identical cloned stools and chairs in strict rows, no variation in angle or placement
Overall sepia/orange grade (concrete wall r73 g51 b36) plus a visible grain/noise overlay; the concrete reads beige, not warm grey
Banquette foreground nearly black (median 18), with the upholstery detail lost

changes.problem: Mother EARF's hard spot makes a blown-looking theatrical ellipse on the wall while the globe itself stays dark and opaque.

evidence.measured: lum_median 108.4, p95 198; edge step 68 over 1 px at x~942; globe region 620,10,860,270 median 23.6, p95 51.6

change.to: 70 W, cone 30 deg (tighter, so the light passes through the discs and lands as a smaller globe shadow, not a wall-wide ellipse)

changes.expected: A smaller, dimmer pool on the concrete with the globe's disc shadows readable inside it; the wall stops competing with the bar top.

changes.problem: The globe's 25 mm cast discs show no glowing polished edges and read as dark sheet; the centrepiece is invisible.

change.setting: Domes' downlights / haze (light that reaches the globe)
change.from: haze 0.007 per m; globe lit only by its own spot
change.to: haze 0.012 per m, so the spot beam through the globe becomes visible; add a low grazing light on the disc edges if the rig allows it (e.g. retarget one Dome downlight to clip the globe's lower edge)

changes.expected: Disc edges pick up bright lines and the smoke tint shows against the beams; the globe reads as acrylic, not as a black cage.

changes.problem: The whole frame carries a sepia/orange cast, so the concrete reads beige and the room is not neutral.

change.to: 2850 (closer to the 2400-2700 K sources, which neutralises them toward warm grey)

changes.expected: Concrete becomes a warm grey and timber stays warm; the smoked products separate from the room.

changes.problem: The Domes' downlights over-light the floor and bar top, which makes the floor blotchy and bright for a night room.

evidence.measured: floor lum_median 84.4, p95 190.7; bar top 0,420,420,490 median 144.9, p95 235

change.to: 4 x spot 50 W, cone 24 deg; and drop the floor's polish (roughness up) so the stool shadows stop stacking into a caustic pattern

changes.expected: Pools on the counter, falling off to a darker floor; floor median about 45 to 65.

changes.problem: The framed screens on the right wall read as flat, blank pink-grey light boxes.
changes.expected: The screens sit back into the wall as dim images and are no longer the second-brightest surface.

changes.problem: No EARF product is the hero: the altar pair is about 40 px wide each and the globe is cut into the ceiling.

evidence.measured: speaker regions lum_median 44.8 and 42.0; each about 3.5% of the frame's width

change.to: 35 mm, aimed at about [12.0, 2.6, 1.6], so the globe sits fully in the upper third and the altar grows in frame

changes.expected: Globe and altar pair both read at a glance; less dead ceiling.

changes.problem: The altar speakers are below the brief's 45 floor and read as white boxes, not tinted acrylic.

change.to: 2 x 220 W, cone 22 deg, aimed slightly behind the cabinets to light through the smoked acrylic

changes.expected: The cabinets show their smoke tint and edge glow; speaker regions at a median of 50 or more.

changes.problem: The foreground lacks signs of life, and the cloned stools in perfect rows read as instanced.

evidence.measured: identical stools at identical angles; foreground table carries only one rocks glass

change.to: rotate the stools 5 to 15 deg each, one pulled out; put a record and sleeve and a menu on the foreground table; drape a coat on the near chair

changes.expected: A lived-in, used room, not a showroom.

out_of_scope.request: Give the Orbs and the speakers more visible tint so a saturated colour appears in the frame
out_of_scope.why: The configuration is Smoke and the products' colour is fixed; the frame will stay near-monochrome by design

out_of_scope.request: Vary the repeated stool and table models
out_of_scope.why: The seats and furniture are fixed by the room's design; only their placement can vary
